methodologyNotes: Covers standalone digital-to-analog converters and headphone amplifiers, including combined DAC/amp units, sold at a published US MSRP — desktop boxes, portable/battery units, and USB dongles. Excludes AV receivers, integrated stereo/speaker amplifiers, powered speakers, and multi-channel pro-audio interfaces. Price is typical US MSRP in USD. formFactor is one of desktop, portable, or dongle. dacChip is the converter make and model as printed on the spec sheet (e.g., ES9038Q2M, AK4493S), or the technology name for custom parts (e.g., FPGA, R2R). maxPcmKhz is the highest PCM sample rate accepted over USB, in kHz. maxDsd is the highest native DSD rate as a DSD multiple (e.g., DSD256); null if DSD is unsupported. maxPowerMw is the rated maximum output power per channel into a 32-ohm load from the most powerful (balanced, where fitted) headphone output, in mW; null for DAC-only units with no headphone output. snrDb is the manufacturer A-weighted signal-to-noise ratio in dB (higher is better). thdnPercent is the best-case manufacturer THD+N figure as a percentage (lower is better). balancedOutput is true if a balanced headphone output (4.4mm or 4-pin XLR) is present. headphoneJacks lists headphone connector types present, slash-delimited (e.g., 6.35mm/4.4mm), or 'none' for DAC-only units. digitalInputs lists digital input types, slash-delimited (e.g., USB-C/optical/coaxial/Bluetooth). weightGrams is unit weight in grams.

products.name: FiiO K11
products.priceNote: Bloom Audio (US authorized retailer) lists "Regular price $142.99" for the FiiO K11 (Black); the page's variant JSON confirms "price":14299 (cents) = $142.99. No US price is published on FiiO's own K11 pages.
products.provenance: FiiO's official K11 parameters page confirms the exact model (K11 with DAC CS43198, distinct from the sibling K11 R2R) and lists a desktop unit with 384kHz-32bit PCM/DSD256 over USB, headline SNR ≥123dB (A-weighted), best-case line-out THD+N <0.00035%, a 4.4mm balanced output rated L+R≥1400mW+1400mW into 32Ω, a 6.35mm headphone jack, USB Type-C/optical/coaxial digital inputs, and ~407g weight. Bloom Audio's retailer listing corroborates the same CS43198 DAC, 1400mW output, 384kHz/32bit PCM/DSD256, ≥123dB SNR, and <0.00035% THD+N, and supplies the US price: "Regular price $142.99" (variant JSON price 14299 cents). No release date is stated on either fetched page, so releaseDate is null.

products.name: iFi Zen DAC 3
products.priceNote: Apos Audio (US retailer) lists "Sale price $229.00 USD" for the "iFi ZEN DAC 3 Desktop DAC" — this is the standard US price/MSRP. The manufacturer store (ifi-audio.com) shows only the EU price of €249,00, so the USD figure is sourced from the corroboration page.
products.provenance: The official iFi audio product page (ifi-audio.com/products/zen-dac-3) confirmed model identity as the "ZEN DAC 3" and provided the spec sheet: Burr-Brown True Native DAC, PCM to 768kHz / DSD512, USB Type-C input, balanced 4.4mm plus single-ended 6.35mm headphone outputs, MAXIMUM OUTPUT POWER BAL 4.4mm ">300mW @ 32Ω", and NET WEIGHT 456g; it lists the line-section figure as DNR ≥113dBA. Apos Audio (US retailer) corroborated the exact model as the "iFi ZEN DAC 3 Desktop DAC", supplied the US price of $229.00 USD, and provided the THD+N figure (<0.005% BAL, best case) and labeled the ≥113 dBA (line) figure as "DNR/SNR". No release date was stated on either fetched page, so releaseDate is null.

products.name: Chord Mojo 2
products.priceNote: HeadAmp (authorized US retailer, headamp.com) lists "Chord Mojo 2 DAC / Portable Amp" at "$650.00" (page updated May 28, 2026). The UK manufacturer page publishes no US price.
products.provenance: The official Chord Electronics Mojo 2 product page confirms this exact model — a portable, custom-coded FPGA-based DAC/headphone amplifier — and its published spec: "Supports up to 768kHz", "Up to DSD 256 (4x)", power output "600 mW 30 ohms" / "90 mW 300 ohms", "Signal to noise: 123dB 'A' weighted", "Distortion and noise 0.0003 %", "1x 3.5 mm/1x 4.4 mm headphone output", five digital inputs (USB-C/Micro-USB/optical/coaxial) and "weight: 185 g". HeadAmp, an authorized US retailer, corroborates the same current model ("the latest Mojo2 with 3.5mm and 4.4mm headphone outputs"), the identical 600mW@30ohm / 90mW@300ohm power figures and FPGA processor, describes the headphone jacks as "Single Ended" (so balancedOutput=false), and lists the US price at "$650.00". Price and model identity are both verified against the retailer page; maxPowerMw uses the manufacturer's 30-ohm rating (the nearest published low-impedance figure, verbatim on both pages).

products.name: Topping DX5 II
products.priceNote: US retail price $299. Apos Audio product page lists "Sale price $299.00 USD" and ShenzhenAudio lists "Regular/Sale price $299.00 USD". The TOPPING official store shows the same figure in euros (€299,00).
products.provenance: The TOPPING official store product page confirms the exact model "TOPPING DX5 II" with dual ES9039Q2M DACs, X-Hybrid balanced amp, USB input via XMOS XU316 supporting PCM768kHz/32bit and DSD512, 6.35mm single-ended / 4.4mm balanced / 4-Pin XLR outputs, and "USB, Coaxial SPDIF, Optical SPDIF, and Bluetooth" inputs. The Apos Audio retailer page corroborates the same model and full spec sheet — DAC chip Dual ES9039Q2M, THD+N <0.00006%, SNR 133dB, 6400mW x2 @32Ω balanced — and lists the US price as "Sale price $299.00 USD" (also matched verbatim by ShenzhenAudio). Both describe the DX5 II as the successor to the DX5, confirming model identity; unit weight is not published on either page, so weightGrams is null.

products.name: Schiit Magni Unity
products.priceNote: US MSRP for the base unit (No DAC) as listed on the official Schiit product page: "$119.00". The Sound Advocate review (May 12, 2025) corroborates: "$119 without DAC card". The optional Mesh/Unison USB DAC card raises the price to $199 per the official page (the review lists $189); the base amp price of $119 is used here.
products.provenance: The official Schiit Audio product page confirms this is the Magni Unity (the 5th-generation "Magni 5", introduced as a single modular Magni "for the first time since 2017") and lists the base price as "$119.00" (No DAC), rising to $199 with the optional internal Mesh DAC card; it states Maximum Power into 32 ohms of 2.5W RMS per channel (given verbatim as "2500mW"), THD+N "Less than 0.0001%", SNR "Greater than 122dB", a single-ended 1/4" TRS (6.35mm) headphone output with no balanced jack, and a weight of "2 lb". The dated Sound Advocate review (May 12, 2025) independently reproduces the identical spec sheet verbatim and confirms pricing of "$119 without DAC card / $189 with DAC card", verifying the exact model identity. DAC-specific fields (dacChip, maxPcmKhz, maxDsd, digitalInputs) are left null because they belong to the optional add-on DAC card rather than the base $119 amp being catalogued, and weightGrams is null because only pounds (not grams) are published.

products.name: JDS Labs Element IV
products.priceNote: US MSRP $549.00 for the base "Default Knob" configuration, listed verbatim on the JDS Labs official product page (Silver Edition is a +$598.00 cosmetic variant). Corroborated by the ecoustics dated review, which states "$549 at JDS Labs" and repeatedly cites the $549 price.
products.provenance: The JDS Labs official product page confirms the exact model "Element IV" at a base US MSRP of $549.00 and supplies the full spec sheet: Max Continuous Power @ 32 Ω = 3.2 W (stated elsewhere on the page as "3200 mW per channel"), Signal to Noise Ratio 120 dB, THD+N < 0.00025%, USB PCM to 384 kHz with DSD64-128, a single 6.35mm (1/4") headphone output, USB Type C + optical TOSLINK inputs, and weight "0.57 kg" (570 g). The ecoustics dated review independently corroborates the $549 price, 3.2 W into 32 ohms, SINAD 118 dB / SNR 120 dB / THD+N < 0.00025%, 32-bit/384kHz PCM and DSD128, and the single-ended 6.35mm output (4.4mm balanced only on custom request), and identifies the converter as an ESS Sabre ES9018K2M — a chip JDS does not print on its own spec sheet but which is further corroborated by ear-fidelity and the headphones.com teardown as an ESS Sabre design. Model identity is unambiguous: both pages describe the "Element IV" specifically, distinct from the Element III, with the Silver Edition being only a $598 cosmetic option.

products.name: AudioQuest DragonFly Cobalt
products.priceNote: US MSRP. The Home Studio Basics review (dated 2025-01-15) states the DragonFly Cobalt's original US retail was "around $300" and refers to "its original asking price of $300". The exact launch MSRP of $299.95 does not appear verbatim on any page I fetched, so I report the sourced figure $300. That review's spec table lists a current street price of $179.97. The official AudioQuest page is EUR-only (EUR199.95) and lists no USD price.
products.provenance: The official AudioQuest product page (source) confirms model identity as the DragonFly Cobalt (SKU DRAGONFLYCOBG, UPC 092592098398) and states the ESS ES9038Q2M DAC chip, resolution up to 24-bit/96kHz, 2.1V output, and a USB-A connection; because its storefront is EUR-only (EUR199.95), no USD price was taken from it. The corroborating Home Studio Basics review (dated 2025-01-15) confirms the same model and its single 3.5mm output ("3.5mm jack doubles as a headphone output and line out"), the ES9038Q2M chip, 24-bit/96kHz resolution, and states the original US retail was "around $300" / "its original asking price of $300" (current street ~$179.97), which is the basis for priceUsd=300. Manufacturer SNR, THD+N, per-channel output power in mW, native DSD support, and unit weight in grams were not stated on any fetched page (only a 2.1V output figure and Amazon's packaged 4.2 oz weight, neither of which is the required unit), so those keys are null.

products.name: SMSL DO100
products.priceNote: US price $239 (launch MSRP). Sourced verbatim from the dated Headfonics DO100 review ("It is priced at $239.") and corroborated by the Headfonia review ("a compact desktop DAC selling for $239 USD"). The manufacturer product page lists no price; Amazon/Aoshida list prices are JS-rendered and were not captured verbatim, so $239 is the defensible sourced figure (the unit has since street-discounted below MSRP, but no lower price was verbatim-sourced from a fetched static page).
products.provenance: The SMSL manufacturer page (id/789) confirms this is the exact DO100 — a "Bluetooth Audio DAC" with two ES9038Q2M chips, 2nd-generation XMOS supporting native DSD512 and PCM up to 32bit/768kHz, single-ended RCA plus balanced XLR line outputs and USB/optical/coaxial/Bluetooth inputs, with no headphone output (the HO100 is the separate headphone amp), which distinguishes it from the DO100 Pro (ES9039Q2M) and the larger DO200. The dated Headfonics review confirms the same model ("new SMSL DO100 DAC... capable of up to DSD512"), states the price verbatim as $239, and gives THD+N as 0.00008%. SNR (XLR 126dB) appears on the Amazon and Audiophonics spec tables but not on the manufacturer or Headfonics pages, so snrDb is left null to avoid an unverifiable figure; maxPowerMw and headphoneJacks reflect the unit being DAC-only, and weightGrams is null because only an approximate "0.6 Kilograms" (not a gram figure) was available.
